samples.summary: Slides text-box `insertLink` selection branch was not mirrored: the exact-cover rewrite is missing, so the two editors diverge on Part A
samples.evidence: The todo (docs/tasks/active/20260907-docs-link-text-and-snap-todo.md:15-27) requires `linkTextFollowsHref`/the in-place rewrite to be "shared so the two editors cannot diverge" and "Mirror in packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts". editor.ts gained a `linkRunCoveringRange(...)` + `rewriteLinkHrefInPlace(...)` branch in its *selection* path (editor.ts:3607-3631) precisely because Part B's snap turns a drag over a link into a selection that exactly covers it. text-box-editor.ts:1187-1193 still does `docStore.snapshot(); doc.applyInlineStyle(range, { href: url })` with no covering-run check — and the snapping itself IS active there, since the text box drives the same `TextEditor` (text-box-editor.ts:668) and therefore `setSnappedRange`. So in a slides text box the URL-derived label goes stale exactly as before whenever the link was selected by drag/double-click. Cost is latent today only because slides' link UI is unwired (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/slides-view.tsx:738-741), which the todo itself notes; the divergence defeats the stated reason for putting the helper in link-run.ts.

samples.summary: Snapping was wired into gestures the spec did not list (double/triple-click word+paragraph select, header/footer drag), extending the "accepted consequences" beyond what the issue enumerated
samples.evidence: Part B's wiring checklist is explicit: "Wire at store time, not read time: drag update + shift+click extend (body and in-cell)" (todo:53-54). The diff additionally routes double-click word select (text-editor.ts:2068, 2000), triple-click paragraph select (2056, 1990) and the header/footer drag branch (2239) through `setSnappedRange`. The word-select case is a real user-visible behaviour change not covered by the todo's "Accepted consequences" list (todo:60-64): double-clicking inside `https://example.com` now selects the entire link, so typing over it destroys the whole link rather than one URL segment. Defensible as upholding the invariant, but it is unrequested scope whose consequences were never weighed in the issue.
searchedFor: grep setSnappedRange call sites in text-editor.ts

samples.summary: New cross-cutting selection semantics ("a hyperlink is an atomic unit for pointer selections") and the new `Selection.rawAnchor` state are not recorded in any design doc
samples.evidence: The change introduces a durable selection rule plus new selection state (`packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts` rawAnchor) and a new snapping stage in the pointer pipeline. The analogous precedent, merged-cell range expansion, IS documented (docs/design/docs/tables/docs-table-copy-paste.md:33 references `expandCellRangeForMerges()`), and hyperlink behaviour is otherwise only a ✅ row in docs/design/docs/docs-wordprocessor-roadmap.md:52. No doc under docs/design/docs/ mentions link snapping or rawAnchor; the reasoning lives only in a task/lessons file under docs/tasks/active/, which is not the canonical subsystem doc. Cost stays inside the codebase (behaviour ships as specified), hence minor.

samples.summary: Popover Apply guard ships an inline error-message UI beyond the checklist's "require the caret to still be in one"
samples.evidence: todo:28-31 asks only that Apply be gated when edit mode was entered on an existing link. The diff adds `applyError` state, a layout restructure of edit mode into a column with a `role="alert"` line, and clearing-on-typing. Reasonable UX and justified in the lessons file, but it is unrequested surface (new copy string, new markup) rather than the minimal guard; also note the guard keys on href equality, so two distinct links sharing one href are indistinguishable to it.
